````math
## Appendix A Additional constraint of the convex problem of Erdős minimum overlap problem

Our program for the Erdős minimum overlap constant $`C_{6.5}`$ takes
White’s convex program ([White, 2022](#bib.bib7)) as its base and adds
two positive-semidefinite constraints discovered by the loop. We treat
White’s program as given and refer the reader to [White
(2022)](#bib.bib7) for its derivation; this appendix justifies only the
added constraints.

Let $`T_{f}`$ be the Hermitian Toeplitz matrix built from the
trigonometric moments of $`f`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
(T_{f})_{kl}\;=\;\tfrac{1}{4}\,\delta_{kl}\;+\;\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(a_{|k-l|}-\mathrm{i}\,\mathrm{sgn}(k-l)\,b_{|k-l|}\bigr),
``` |  | (15) |

where $`a_{m},b_{m}`$ are the cosine and sine Fourier coefficients of
$`f`$ (so that the $`(k,l)`$ entry depends only on the lag $`k-l`$). The
loop added the pair

|     |                                                        |     |      |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       T_{f}\succeq 0\qquad\text{and}\qquad I-T_{f}\succeq 0.
       ```                                                     |     | (16) |

We show both are valid necessary conditions, i.e. that every admissible
$`f`$ produces moments satisfying
([16](#A1.E16 "Equation 16 ‣ Appendix A Additional constraint of the convex problem of Erdős minimum overlap problem ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"));
adding them therefore tightens the relaxation without excluding any
admissible $`f`$.

###### Proposition A.1.

For every admissible $`f`$, the matrix $`T_{f}`$ of
([15](#A1.E15 "Equation 15 ‣ Appendix A Additional constraint of the convex problem of Erdős minimum overlap problem ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"))
satisfies $`T_{f}\succeq 0`$ and $`I-T_{f}\succeq 0`$.

###### Proof.

By construction $`T_{f}`$ is the moment (Toeplitz) matrix of $`f`$: its
entries are the Fourier coefficients of $`f`$ arranged by lag, so for
any complex vector $`z`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
z^{*}T_{f}z\;=\;\int_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\Bigl|\sum_{k}z_{k}e^{\mathrm{i}k\pi x}\Bigr|^{2}\,dx.
``` |  |

Since $`f\geq 0`$, the integrand is nonnegative, hence
$`z^{*}T_{f}z\geq 0`$ for all $`z`$ and $`T_{f}\succeq 0`$. This is
Bochner’s theorem: a sequence is the moment sequence of a nonnegative
measure iff its Toeplitz form is positive semidefinite.

For the second condition, apply the same argument to the complement
$`g=1-f`$. Because $`f\leq 1`$ we have $`g\geq 0`$, so $`g`$ is also a
nonnegative function and its moment matrix $`T_{g}`$ satisfies
$`T_{g}\succeq 0`$. The constant function $`1`$ has moment matrix equal
to the identity $`I`$ (its only nonzero Fourier coefficient is the
constant term, which contributes the diagonal), and the moment map is
linear, so $`T_{g}=T_{1}-T_{f}=I-T_{f}`$. Hence
$`I-T_{f}=T_{g}\succeq 0`$. ∎

## Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality

This section derives the convex relaxation for the sharp constant
$`C_{6.2}`$ of Problem_6.2.md and proves rigorously that its optimum
$`\Omega^{*}`$ is a valid lower bound, $`C_{6.2}\geq\Omega^{*}`$. The
development follows the same template as White’s program for the Erdős
overlap problem (Section 1): identify the Fourier/moment data of an
admissible $`f`$, prove a list of *necessary* linear and semidefinite
conditions on that data, and observe that the relaxed feasible set
therefore contains every admissible $`f`$.

### B.1 Reduction and normalisation

We seek a lower bound for

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
C_{6.2}=\inf_{f\geq 0}\;\frac{\max_{-1/2\leq t\leq 1/2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}f(t-x)f(x)\,dx}{\big(\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f(x)\,dx\big)^{2}}.
``` |  |

###### Lemma B.1 (Support reduction).

It suffices to bound the infimum over $`f\geq 0`$ with
$`\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq[-1/4,1/4]`$. Concretely, if for all
$`g\geq 0`$ with $`\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq[-1/4,1/4]`$ we have
$`\max_{\lvert t\rvert\leq 1/2}(g*g)(t)\geq C\big(\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}g\big)^{2}`$,
then the same inequality holds for all $`f\geq 0`$.

###### Proof.

Given $`f\geq 0`$, set $`g=f\cdot\mathbf{1}_{[-1/4,1/4]}`$, so
$`0\leq g\leq f`$ and $`\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq[-1/4,1/4]`$. The
denominators agree: $`\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}g=\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f`$. For the
numerator, $`g\leq f`$ and both are nonnegative, so
$`(g*g)(t)=\int g(t-x)g(x)\,dx\leq\int f(t-x)f(x)\,dx=(f*f)(t)`$
pointwise; taking $`\max_{\lvert t\rvert\leq 1/2}`$ preserves the
inequality. Hence
$`\max(f*f)\geq\max(g*g)\geq C(\int g)^{2}=C(\int f)^{2}`$. ∎

By homogeneity we normalise $`\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f=1`$. Writing $`g=f*f`$
and
$`\Omega=\max_{\lvert t\rvert\leq 1/2}(g)(t)=\lVert f*f\rVert_{\infty}`$,
the reduced problem is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S\;=\;\inf_{f}\;\Big\{\,\lVert f*f\rVert_{\infty}\;:\;f\geq 0,\ \int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f=1,\ \operatorname{supp}f\subseteq[-\tfrac{1}{4},\tfrac{1}{4}]\,\Big\},\qquad C_{6.2}=S.
``` |  | (17) |

### B.2 Fourier and moment data

For an admissible $`f`$ define the real Fourier coefficients

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
a_{k}=\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f(x)\cos(2\pi kx)\,dx,\qquad b_{k}=\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f(x)\sin(2\pi kx)\,dx,\qquad k=0,1,\dots,K,
``` |  |

so that $`\hat{f}(k)=a_{k}-ib_{k}`$ and $`\hat{f}(-k)=a_{k}+ib_{k}`$,
with $`a_{0}=\int f=1`$ and $`b_{0}=0`$. Because $`g=f*f`$ has
$`\hat{g}(k)=\hat{f}(k)^{2}`$, the autocorrelation’s spectrum is
determined by $`(a_{k},b_{k})`$.

We also discretise the localisation window into $`2N`$ equal cells
$`I_{j}=\big[-\tfrac{1}{4}+\tfrac{j}{4N},\,-\tfrac{1}{4}+\tfrac{j+1}{4N}\big]`$,
$`j=0,1,\dots,2N-1`$, and set the local masses

|     |                                      |     |
|-----|--------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       p_{j}=\int_{I_{j}}f(x)\,dx\;\geq\;0.
       ```                                   |     |

### B.3 Necessary conditions

#### (1) Mass.

Since the cells partition $`[-1/4,1/4]`$ and $`\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f=1`$,

|     |                                              |     |      |
|-----|----------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       \sum_{j=0}^{2N-1}p_{j}=1,\qquad p_{j}\geq 0.
       ```                                           |     | (18) |

#### (2) Fourier coefficients from local masses.

For each cell define the trigonometric extrema

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
C_{kj}^{-}=\min_{x\in I_{j}}\cos(2\pi kx),\quad C_{kj}^{+}=\max_{x\in I_{j}}\cos(2\pi kx),\quad S_{kj}^{-}=\min_{x\in I_{j}}\sin(2\pi kx),\quad S_{kj}^{+}=\max_{x\in I_{j}}\sin(2\pi kx).
``` |  |

###### Lemma B.2 (Coefficient envelopes).

For every admissible $`f`$ and every $`k`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{j=0}^{2N-1}C_{kj}^{-}p_{j}\;\leq\;a_{k}\;\leq\;\sum_{j=0}^{2N-1}C_{kj}^{+}p_{j},\qquad\sum_{j=0}^{2N-1}S_{kj}^{-}p_{j}\;\leq\;b_{k}\;\leq\;\sum_{j=0}^{2N-1}S_{kj}^{+}p_{j}.
``` |  | (19) |

###### Proof.

Since $`f\geq 0`$ and $`\operatorname{supp}f`$ is partitioned by the
$`I_{j}`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
a_{k}=\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f(x)\cos(2\pi kx)\,dx=\sum_{j}\int_{I_{j}}f(x)\cos(2\pi kx)\,dx.
``` |  |

On each cell, $`C_{kj}^{-}\leq\cos(2\pi kx)\leq C_{kj}^{+}`$ for all
$`x\in I_{j}`$, and $`\int_{I_{j}}f=p_{j}\geq 0`$. Multiplying the
pointwise bounds by the nonnegative density $`f`$ and integrating gives
$`C_{kj}^{-}p_{j}\leq\int_{I_{j}}f\cos(2\pi kx)\,dx\leq C_{kj}^{+}p_{j}`$.
Summing over $`j`$ yields the bound on $`a_{k}`$; the argument for
$`b_{k}`$ is identical with $`\sin`$. ∎

#### (3) Moment matrix.

Let
$`y=(1,a_{1},\dots,a_{K},b_{1},\dots,b_{K})^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{2K+1}`$
and $`M=y\,y^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{(2K+1)\times(2K+1)}`$, indexed
$`0,1,\dots,2K`$.

###### Lemma B.3 (Moment matrix is feasible and rank one).

The matrix $`M=yy^{\top}`$ satisfies $`M\succeq 0`$ and

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
M_{0,0}=1,\quad M_{0,k}=a_{k},\quad M_{0,K+k}=b_{k},\quad M_{k,k}=a_{k}^{2},\quad M_{K+k,K+k}=b_{k}^{2}\quad(1\leq k\leq K).
``` |  |

###### Proof.

$`M=yy^{\top}`$ is a Gram matrix of a single vector, hence PSD:
$`u^{\top}Mu=(y^{\top}u)^{2}\geq 0`$ for all $`u`$. The listed entries
are the corresponding products $`y_{i}y_{j}`$: $`y_{0}=1`$,
$`y_{k}=a_{k}`$, $`y_{K+k}=b_{k}`$, so $`M_{0,0}=1`$, $`M_{0,k}=a_{k}`$,
$`M_{0,K+k}=b_{k}`$, $`M_{k,k}=a_{k}^{2}`$, $`M_{K+k,K+k}=b_{k}^{2}`$. ∎

In the relaxation we keep only the convex consequences: $`M\succeq 0`$,
the affine entry constraints of
Lemma [B.3](#A2.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma B.3 (Moment matrix is feasible and rank one). ‣ (3) Moment matrix. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")
linking the first row/diagonal to $`(a,b)`$, and the envelopes
([19](#A2.E19 "Equation 19 ‣ Lemma B.2 (Coefficient envelopes). ‣ (2) Fourier coefficients from local masses. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")).
We do *not* impose $`\operatorname{rank}M=1`$ (nonconvex). Every
admissible $`f`$ produces a feasible $`M`$, so no admissible point is
lost.

#### (4) The objective bound via Parseval.

###### Lemma B.4 (Spectral lower bound on $`\Omega`$).

Let $`w_{k}=1-\tfrac{k}{K+1}\in[0,1)`$ be the Fejér weights. For
admissible $`f`$ with $`\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f=1`$, the sharp identity is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Omega\;=\;\lVert f*f\rVert_{\infty}\;\geq\;1+2\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\big(a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2}\big)^{2},
``` |  | (20) |

and consequently the weighted, truncated relaxation used by the program
holds:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Omega\;\geq\;1+2\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\,v_{k},\qquad\text{where}\quad v_{k}\geq\big(M_{k,k}+M_{K+k,K+k}\big)^{2}=(a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2})^{2}.
``` |  | (21) |

###### Proof.

Let $`g=f*f\geq 0`$ (nonnegative as a self-convolution of $`f\geq 0`$).
Its total mass is $`\int_{\mathbb{R}}g=\big(\int f\big)^{2}=1`$.
Therefore
$`\Omega=\lVert g\rVert_{\infty}=\lVert g\rVert_{\infty}\int g\geq\int g^{2}`$,
since $`\int g^{2}\leq\lVert g\rVert_{\infty}\int g`$ for $`g\geq 0`$.
By Parseval and $`\hat{g}(m)=\hat{f}(m)^{2}`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\int g^{2}=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}\lvert\hat{g}(m)\rvert^{2}=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}\lvert\hat{f}(m)\rvert^{4}=1+2\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}(a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2})^{2},
``` |  |

using $`\hat{f}(0)=1`$ and
$`\lvert\hat{f}(\pm k)\rvert^{2}=a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2}`$. This proves
([20](#A2.E20 "Equation 20 ‣ Lemma B.4 (Spectral lower bound on Ω). ‣ (4) The objective bound via Parseval. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")).
For
([21](#A2.E21 "Equation 21 ‣ Lemma B.4 (Spectral lower bound on Ω). ‣ (4) The objective bound via Parseval. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")):
every term $`(a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2})^{2}\geq 0`$ and
$`0\leq w_{k}\leq 1`$, so

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
1+2\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}(a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2})^{2}\;\leq\;1+2\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}(a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2})^{2}\;\leq\;\Omega.
``` |  |

With $`a_{k}^{2}=M_{k,k}`$, $`b_{k}^{2}=M_{K+k,K+k}`$
(Lemma [B.3](#A2.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma B.3 (Moment matrix is feasible and rank one). ‣ (3) Moment matrix. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"))
and the epigraph variable $`v_{k}\geq(M_{k,k}+M_{K+k,K+k})^{2}`$, the
left side is exactly the program’s constraint. The weights and
truncation only *weaken* the bound, so it remains a valid lower bound on
$`\Omega`$. ∎

### B.4 The three positive-semidefinite blocks

The program contains three Hermitian PSD blocks, each of size $`K+1`$
and each the real embedding of a Hermitian Toeplitz matrix. We verify
all three from the quadratic-form/Bochner principle: a Hermitian
Toeplitz matrix $`T=(\tau_{i-j})`$ is positive semidefinite whenever its
symbol $`\tau_{k}=\int w(x)e^{-2\pi ikx}\,dx`$ arises from a
*nonnegative* weight $`w`$, because then for all
$`z\in\mathbb{C}^{K+1}`$

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
z^{*}Tz=\sum_{i,j}\bar{z}_{i}\,\tau_{i-j}\,z_{j}=\int w(x)\,\Big|\sum_{j=0}^{K}z_{j}e^{2\pi ijx}\Big|^{2}dx\geq 0.
``` |  | (22) |

The three blocks differ only in the choice of nonnegative weight $`w`$.

#### (5a) Plain Bochner–Toeplitz on $`f`$.

Recall $`\hat{f}(k)=a_{k}-ib_{k}`$ (with
$`\hat{f}(-k)=\overline{\hat{f}(k)}`$), and form the Hermitian Toeplitz
$`T_{f}`$ with $`(T_{f})_{ij}=\hat{f}(i-j)`$, i.e. real part
$`a_{\lvert i-j\rvert}`$ and imaginary part $`-b_{\lvert i-j\rvert}`$
for $`i>j`$, $`+b_{\lvert i-j\rvert}`$ for $`i<j`$, diagonal
$`a_{0}=1`$. In the program this is the big block.

###### Lemma B.5 (Plain Bochner block).

$`T_{f}\succeq 0`$.

###### Proof.

Apply
([22](#A2.E22 "Equation 22 ‣ B.4 The three positive-semidefinite blocks ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"))
with weight $`w=f\geq 0`$: the symbol is
$`\tau_{k}=\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f(x)e^{-2\pi ikx}\,dx=\hat{f}(k)=a_{k}-ib_{k}`$,
which are precisely the entries of $`T_{f}`$. Hence
$`z^{*}T_{f}z=\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f(x)\,\big|\sum_{j}z_{j}e^{2\pi ijx}\big|^{2}dx\geq 0`$
since $`f\geq 0`$. ∎

#### (5b) Localised Bochner with $`h(x)=\cos(2\pi x)`$.

Form the Hermitian Toeplitz $`T_{\nu}`$ with symbol $`\nu_{k}`$, where,
writing $`\operatorname{sgn}`$ for the sign function,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\operatorname{Re}\nu_{k}=\tfrac{1}{2}\big(a_{\lvert k-1\rvert}+a_{\lvert k+1\rvert}\big),\qquad\operatorname{Im}\nu_{k}=-\tfrac{1}{2}\big(\operatorname{sgn}(k-1)\,b_{\lvert k-1\rvert}+\operatorname{sgn}(k+1)\,b_{\lvert k+1\rvert}\big).
``` |  |

In the program this is the big_nu block, assembled from nu_re and nu_im.

###### Lemma B.6 (Localised Bochner block).

Define $`\nu_{k}`$ by the affine maps
$`\operatorname{Re}\nu_{k}=\tfrac{1}{2}(a_{\lvert k-1\rvert}+a_{\lvert k+1\rvert})`$,
$`\operatorname{Im}\nu_{k}=-\tfrac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sgn}(k-1)\,b_{\lvert k-1\rvert}+\operatorname{sgn}(k+1)\,b_{\lvert k+1\rvert})`$,
and let $`T_{\nu}=(\nu_{i-j})_{i,j=0}^{K}`$. Then:

1.  (i)
    $`\nu_{k}`$ equals the $`k`$-th Fourier coefficient of
    $`x\mapsto\cos(2\pi x)f(x)`$;
2.  (ii)
    $`\nu_{-k}=\overline{\nu_{k}}`$, so $`T_{\nu}`$ is Hermitian
    Toeplitz; equivalently $`\operatorname{Re}T_{\nu}`$ is symmetric and
    $`\operatorname{Im}T_{\nu}`$ is skew-symmetric, which is exactly the
    structure required for the real embedding
    $`\big[\begin{smallmatrix}\operatorname{Re}T_{\nu}&-\operatorname{Im}T_{\nu}\\
    \operatorname{Im}T_{\nu}&\operatorname{Re}T_{\nu}\end{smallmatrix}\big]`$
    to represent $`T_{\nu}`$;
3.  (iii)
    the program imposes the single semidefinite constraint
    $`T_{\nu}\succeq 0`$ (no trace or band-sum equalities are attached
    to this block), and $`T_{\nu}\succeq 0`$ holds for every admissible
    $`f`$.

###### Proof.

*(i)* Since $`\cos(2\pi x)=\tfrac{1}{2}(e^{2\pi ix}+e^{-2\pi ix})`$,
multiplication by $`\cos(2\pi x)`$ shifts Fourier coefficients by
$`\pm 1`$:
$`\widehat{\cos(2\pi\cdot)f}(k)=\tfrac{1}{2}(\hat{f}(k-1)+\hat{f}(k+1))`$.
Using
$`\hat{f}(m)=a_{\lvert m\rvert}-i\,\operatorname{sgn}(m)\,b_{\lvert m\rvert}`$
for all $`m\in\mathbb{Z}`$ (with $`\hat{f}(0)=a_{0}`$ real), the real
part of $`\tfrac{1}{2}(\hat{f}(k-1)+\hat{f}(k+1))`$ is
$`\tfrac{1}{2}(a_{\lvert k-1\rvert}+a_{\lvert k+1\rvert})`$ and the
imaginary part is
$`-\tfrac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sgn}(k-1)b_{\lvert k-1\rvert}+\operatorname{sgn}(k+1)b_{\lvert k+1\rvert})`$,
matching $`\nu_{k}`$ exactly.

*(ii)* From (i),
$`\nu_{-k}=\widehat{\cos(2\pi\cdot)f}(-k)=\overline{\widehat{\cos(2\pi\cdot)f}(k)}=\overline{\nu_{k}}`$
because $`\cos(2\pi x)f(x)`$ is real-valued. Hence
$`(T_{\nu})_{ji}=\nu_{j-i}=\nu_{-(i-j)}=\overline{\nu_{i-j}}=\overline{(T_{\nu})_{ij}}`$,
so $`T_{\nu}`$ is Hermitian; writing
$`T_{\nu}=\operatorname{Re}T_{\nu}+i\operatorname{Im}T_{\nu}`$,
$`\operatorname{Re}T_{\nu}`$ is symmetric and
$`\operatorname{Im}T_{\nu}`$ is skew-symmetric, which is precisely what
makes the real embedding a faithful representation (its spectrum is that
of $`T_{\nu}`$ doubled).

*(iii)* Apply
([22](#A2.E22 "Equation 22 ‣ B.4 The three positive-semidefinite blocks ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"))
with weight $`w(x)=\cos(2\pi x)f(x)`$:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
z^{*}T_{\nu}z=\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}\cos(2\pi x)\,f(x)\,\Big|\sum_{j=0}^{K}z_{j}e^{2\pi ijx}\Big|^{2}dx.
``` |  |

On $`\operatorname{supp}f=[-1/4,1/4]`$ we have
$`2\pi\lvert x\rvert\leq\pi/2`$, so $`\cos(2\pi x)\geq 0`$ throughout
the support of $`f`$; the integrand is therefore nonnegative and
$`z^{*}T_{\nu}z\geq 0`$. ∎

###### Remark B.7.

The localiser $`h(x)=\cos(2\pi x)`$ is chosen precisely because its
first nonnegativity interval $`[-1/4,1/4]`$ coincides with
$`\operatorname{supp}f`$. Any $`h\geq 0`$ on $`[-1/4,1/4]`$ whose
Fourier support is bounded would furnish a valid localised block;
$`\cos(2\pi x)`$ is the simplest single-frequency choice and gives the
$`\pm 1`$ coefficient shift above.

#### (5c) Fejér–Riesz block $`Q`$ for the autocorrelation.

Let $`g=f*f`$, so
$`\hat{g}(k)=\hat{f}(k)^{2}=(a_{k}-ib_{k})^{2}=(a_{k}^{2}-b_{k}^{2})-i\,(2a_{k}b_{k})`$,
and let $`F_{K}`$ be the $`K`$-th Fejér kernel with weights
$`w_{k}=1-\tfrac{k}{K+1}`$, $`F_{K}\geq 0`$, $`\int F_{K}=1`$. Define
$`Q`$ as the Hermitian Toeplitz matrix with symbol

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
q_{0}=\Omega-1,\qquad q_{k}=-\,w_{k}\,\hat{g}(k)\ \ (1\leq k\leq K),
``` |  |

in the program this is the Q block (the constraints
$`\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}Q=\Omega-1`$ and the banded
real/imaginary identities).

###### Lemma B.8 (Fejér–Riesz block).

Let $`z(t)=(1,e^{it},\dots,e^{iKt})^{\!\top}`$ and let $`Q`$ be the
Hermitian $`(K+1)\times(K+1)`$ Gram matrix of the localised symbol
$`h(t)=\Omega-(F_{K}*g)(t)`$, i.e. $`h(t)=z(t)^{*}Q\,z(t)`$. With $`M`$
the rank-one moment matrix of
Lemma [B.3](#A2.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma B.3 (Moment matrix is feasible and rank one). ‣ (3) Moment matrix. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")
(so $`M_{k,k}=a_{k}^{2}`$, $`M_{K+k,K+k}=b_{k}^{2}`$,
$`M_{k,K+k}=a_{k}b_{k}`$), the symbol coefficients
$`q_{k}:=\sum_{l-j=k}Q_{jl}`$ satisfy

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\operatorname{Re}q_{k}=-w_{k}\,(M_{k,k}-M_{K+k,K+k}),\qquad\operatorname{Im}q_{k}=+\,2\,w_{k}\,M_{k,K+k}\qquad(1\leq k\leq K),
``` |  |

the $`k`$-th diagonal sum of $`Q`$ reproducing the program’s banded
constraints. The zeroth constraint is the trace,
$`\operatorname{tr}Q=q_{0}=\Omega-1`$. Moreover $`Q\succeq 0`$.

###### Proof.

Substituting $`\hat{g}(k)=(a_{k}^{2}-b_{k}^{2})-i\,(2a_{k}b_{k})`$ into
$`q_{k}=-w_{k}\hat{g}(k)`$ gives

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\operatorname{Re}q_{k}=-w_{k}(a_{k}^{2}-b_{k}^{2})=-w_{k}(M_{k,k}-M_{K+k,K+k}),\qquad\operatorname{Im}q_{k}=+w_{k}(2a_{k}b_{k})=2w_{k}M_{k,K+k}.
``` |  |

Expanding $`h(t)=z(t)^{*}Qz(t)=\sum_{j,l}Q_{jl}e^{i(l-j)t}`$ and
matching the coefficient of $`e^{ikt}`$ gives
$`\hat{h}(k)=\sum_{l-j=k}Q_{jl}=q_{k}`$, so these are exactly the banded
(diagonal-sum) constraints of the program. For $`k=0`$,
$`\hat{g}(0)=(\int f)^{2}=1`$ and $`w_{0}=1`$, whence
$`q_{0}=\hat{h}(0)=\Omega-\widehat{F_{K}*g}(0)=\Omega-1`$; since the
$`0`$-th diagonal is the main diagonal,
$`\operatorname{tr}Q=q_{0}=\Omega-1`$.

The symbol $`h`$ is a nonnegative trigonometric polynomial of degree
$`K`$: indeed $`g=f*f\geq 0`$ and $`F_{K}\geq 0`$ with $`\int F_{K}=1`$,
so by Jensen/averaging
$`(F_{K}*g)(t)\leq\lVert g\rVert_{\infty}=\Omega`$, giving
$`h=\Omega-F_{K}*g\geq 0`$, while $`\hat{h}(k)=w_{k}\hat{g}(k)`$
vanishes for $`\lvert k\rvert>K`$ since $`w_{k}=0`$ there. By the
Fejér–Riesz theorem there is an analytic polynomial
$`p(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{K}c_{j}e^{ijt}`$ with

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
h(t)=\lvert p(t)\rvert^{2}=z(t)^{*}\,(cc^{*})\,z(t),\qquad c=(c_{0},\dots,c_{K})^{\!\top}.
``` |  |

Hence $`Q=cc^{*}\succeq 0`$ realises the symbol $`h`$ with the
prescribed diagonal sums: it is the Fejér–Riesz certificate, and
$`Q\succeq 0`$ as claimed. ∎

#### Real embedding.

As in Section 1, each Hermitian block $`T=A+iB`$ ($`A`$ symmetric, $`B`$
skew-symmetric) is realised in CVXPY through the real embedding
$`\big[\begin{smallmatrix}A&-B\\
B&A\end{smallmatrix}\big]\succeq 0`$, equivalent to $`T\succeq 0`$
because the embedding’s spectrum is that of $`T`$ with each eigenvalue
doubled. In the program this is the
cp.bmat(\[\[T_R,-T_I\],\[T_I,T_R\]\]) construction, used for all three
Hermitian blocks.

### B.5 The relaxed convex program and its validity

###### Definition B.9 (Relaxation).

With $`g=f*f`$, $`\hat{f}(k)=a_{k}-\mathbf{i}b_{k}`$, Fejér weights
$`w_{k}=1-\tfrac{k}{K+1}`$, and $`\gamma^{\pm}_{k},\sigma^{\pm}_{k}`$
the per-cell lower/upper envelopes of $`\cos(2\pi kx),\sin(2\pi kx)`$,
the value $`\Omega^{*}`$ is the optimum of

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\Omega^{*}=\min_{\Omega,\,p,\,a,\,b,\,M,\,Q,\,v}`$ | $`\displaystyle\Omega`$ |  |  |  | (23) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\text{s.t.}`$ | $`\displaystyle\textstyle\displaystyle\sum_{j}p_{j}=1,\ p_{j}\geq 0`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(mass)}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\gamma^{-}_{k}\!\cdot p\leq a_{k}\leq\gamma^{+}_{k}\!\cdot p,\quad\sigma^{-}_{k}\!\cdot p\leq b_{k}\leq\sigma^{+}_{k}\!\cdot p`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(Lemma \ref{lem:env})}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle M\succeq 0,\ M_{0,0}=1,\ M_{0,k}=a_{k},\ M_{0,K+k}=b_{k}`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(Lemma \ref{lem:M})}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle v_{k}\geq(M_{k,k}+M_{K+k,K+k})^{2},\quad\Omega\geq 1+2\textstyle\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\,v_{k}`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(Lemma \ref{lem:parseval})}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle Q\succeq 0,\ \operatorname{tr}Q=\Omega-1`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(Lemma \ref{lem:Q})}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\textstyle\displaystyle\sum_{i}Q_{i,i+k}=\mathbf{i}\,2w_{k}M_{k,K+k}-w_{k}\bigl(M_{k,k}-M_{K+k,K+k}\bigr)`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(Fej\'{e}r band, Lemma \ref{lem:Q})}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle T_{f}\succeq 0,\quad(T_{f})_{ij}=a_{|i-j|}-\mathbf{i}\,\mathrm{sgn}(i-j)\,b_{|i-j|}`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(Lemma \ref{lem:bochner-f})}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle T_{\nu}\succeq 0,\quad(T_{\nu})_{ij}=\nu_{i-j},\quad\nu_{k}=\tfrac{1}{2}(\hat{\mu}_{k-1}+\hat{\mu}_{k+1})`$ |  | $`\displaystyle\text{(Lemma \ref{lem:bochner-loc})}.`$ |  |  |

The envelope coefficients $`\gamma^{\pm}_{k},\sigma^{\pm}_{k}`$ are
computed by the *analytical* cell extrema of
$`\cos(2\pi kx),\sin(2\pi kx)`$ on each cell (the
cos_extrema_on_cell/sin_extrema_on_cell routines), not a grid sample.
This matters for rigor: a grid minimum over-estimates the true minimum,
which would make $`a_{k}\geq(\text{grid min})\cdot p`$ *stricter* than
correct and could exclude an admissible $`f`$. The analytical extrema
(endpoints together with the interior critical points $`x=m/(2k)`$ for
$`\cos`$ and $`x=(2m+1)/(4k)`$ for $`\sin`$) give the true cell min/max,
so
Lemma [B.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma B.2 (Coefficient envelopes). ‣ (2) Fourier coefficients from local masses. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")
holds exactly.

###### Theorem B.10 (Validity of the relaxation).

$`C_{6.2}=S\geq\Omega^{*}`$.

###### Proof.

Let $`f`$ be any admissible function for the reduced
problem ([17](#A2.E17 "Equation 17 ‣ B.1 Reduction and normalisation ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")):
$`f\geq 0`$, $`\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f=1`$,
$`\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq[-1/4,1/4]`$. We construct a feasible
point
of ([23](#A2.E23 "Equation 23 ‣ Definition B.9 (Relaxation). ‣ B.5 The relaxed convex program and its validity ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"))
with objective value $`\lVert f*f\rVert_{\infty}`$.

Set $`p_{j}=\int_{I_{j}}f`$, $`a_{k},b_{k}`$ the Fourier coefficients of
$`f`$, $`y=(1,a,b)`$, $`M=yy^{\top}`$,
$`\Omega=\lVert f*f\rVert_{\infty}`$,
$`v_{k}=(a_{k}^{2}+b_{k}^{2})^{2}`$, and $`T_{f},T_{\nu},Q`$ the three
Hermitian Toeplitz blocks built from $`f`$’s data. Each constraint
of ([23](#A2.E23 "Equation 23 ‣ Definition B.9 (Relaxation). ‣ B.5 The relaxed convex program and its validity ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"))
is then satisfied:

- •
  the mass constraint
  by ([18](#A2.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ (1) Mass. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents"));
- •
  the coefficient envelopes by
  Lemma [B.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma B.2 (Coefficient envelopes). ‣ (2) Fourier coefficients from local masses. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")
  (analytical cell extrema);
- •
  $`M\succeq 0`$ and its entry identities by
  Lemma [B.3](#A2.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma B.3 (Moment matrix is feasible and rank one). ‣ (3) Moment matrix. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents");
- •
  the objective inequality $`\Omega\geq 1+2\sum_{k}w_{k}v_{k}`$ by
  Lemma [B.4](#A2.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma B.4 (Spectral lower bound on Ω). ‣ (4) The objective bound via Parseval. ‣ B.3 Necessary conditions ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents");
- •
  $`T_{f}\succeq 0`$ by
  Lemma [B.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma B.5 (Plain Bochner block). ‣ (5a) Plain Bochner–Toeplitz on 𝑓. ‣ B.4 The three positive-semidefinite blocks ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")
  (weight $`f\geq 0`$);
- •
  $`T_{\nu}\succeq 0`$ by
  Lemma [B.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma B.6 (Localised Bochner block). ‣ (5b) Localised Bochner with ℎ(𝑥)=cos(2⁢𝜋⁢𝑥). ‣ B.4 The three positive-semidefinite blocks ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")
  (weight $`\cos(2\pi x)f\geq 0`$ on $`\operatorname{supp}f`$);
- •
  $`Q\succeq 0`$ and the Fejér band identities by
  Lemma [B.8](#A2.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma B.8 (Fejér–Riesz block). ‣ (5c) Fejér–Riesz block 𝑄 for the autocorrelation. ‣ B.4 The three positive-semidefinite blocks ‣ Appendix B Derivation of the convex problem of the First Autocorrelation Inequality ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")
  (weight $`\Omega-F_{K}*g\geq 0`$).

Every one of these is a *necessary* condition - proved above for an
arbitrary admissible $`f`$, not merely for an optimiser - so the
constructed point is feasible. Its objective is
$`\Omega=\lVert f*f\rVert_{\infty}`$. Therefore

|     |                                          |     |
|-----|------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \Omega^{*}\leq\lVert f*f\rVert_{\infty}.
       ```                                       |     |

Taking the infimum over all admissible $`f`$ gives
$`\Omega^{*}\leq S=C_{6.2}`$, i.e. $`\Omega^{*}`$ is a valid lower
bound. ∎

## Appendix C Floating point precision details

A numerical conic solver returns an approximate primal–dual pair that is
in general neither exactly feasible nor exactly optimal, and is computed
in floating-point arithmetic on data that is itself a floating-point
rounding of the intended (rational/real) problem. To turn the solver
output into a *mathematically rigorous* lower bound we use a certified
weak-duality argument: we verify in directed-rounding interval
arithmetic that a candidate dual point lies in the dual cone, and charge
every rounding and data error to a penalty controlled by an a-priori
bound on the primal solution norm.

### C.1 Canonical primal and dual

Our certified-duality method relies on the canonicalisation produced by
CVXPY for the SCS standard form. After canonicalisation the primal is

|     |                                                             |     |      |
|-----|-------------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       \min_{x}\;c^{\top}x\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Ax+s=b,\ \ s\in K,
       ```                                                          |     | (24) |

with the product cone
$`K=K_{\mathrm{zero}}\times K_{\geq 0}\times K_{\mathrm{SOC}}\times K_{\mathrm{PSD}}`$
in exactly that order. The Lagrangian dual is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\max_{y}\;-b^{\top}y\quad\text{s.t.}\quad A^{\top}y+c=0,\ \ y\in K^{*},
``` |  | (25) |

where $`K^{*}`$ is the dual cone (here $`K^{*}=K`$ blockwise, except the
zero cone dualises to the free cone). For any dual-feasible $`y`$, weak
duality gives $`-b^{\top}y\leq c^{\top}x^{*}=\Omega^{*}`$, so a
rigorously dual-feasible $`y`$ certifies the lower bound $`-b^{\top}y`$.

### C.2 Error model and the master certificate

The stored data $`(A,b,c)`$ are floating-point; the intended data are
$`(\hat{A},\hat{b},\hat{c})`$, with rigorous outward-rounded elementwise
error bounds

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\max_{ij}\lvert A_{ij}-\hat{A}_{ij}\rvert\leq\varepsilon_{A},\qquad\max_{i}\lvert b_{i}-\hat{b}_{i}\rvert\leq\varepsilon_{b},\qquad\max_{j}\lvert c_{j}-\hat{c}_{j}\rvert\leq\varepsilon_{c}.
``` |  |

We estimate $`\varepsilon_{A},\varepsilon_{b}`$ and $`\varepsilon_{c}`$
by using mpmath arbitrary-precision library and verify that for our
problem sizes, $`\epsilon_{A},\epsilon_{b},\epsilon_{c}\leq 1e-12`$.

Now we show how we can get a certified lower bound.

###### Theorem C.1 (Certified lower bound).

Let $`y`$ be verified to lie in $`K^{*}`$
(Algorithm [3](#alg3 "Algorithm 3 ‣ C.4 Rigorous certificate of dual-cone containment ‣ Appendix C Floating point precision details ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")).
Let $`r\geq\lVert A^{\top}y+c\rVert_{\infty}`$ be an outward-rounded
upper bound on the floating dual-feasibility residual and
$`X\geq\lVert x^{*}\rVert_{1}`$ an a-priori bound
(Section [C.3](#A3.SS3 "C.3 A-priori bound on ∥𝑥^∗∥_1 ‣ Appendix C Floating point precision details ‣ AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents")).
With

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tot}}=r+\varepsilon_{A}\lVert y\rVert_{1}+\varepsilon_{c},\qquad\Pi=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tot}}\,X+\varepsilon_{b}\,\lVert y\rVert_{1},
``` |  |

one has

|     |                                                                    |     |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \Omega^{*}\;\geq\;L\;:=\;(-b^{\top}y)_{\downarrow}-\Pi_{\uparrow},
       ```                                                                 |     |

computed with directed rounding ($`\downarrow`$ down, $`\uparrow`$ up).

###### Proof.

Let $`x^{*}`$ be any optimiser of the intended primal, so
$`\hat{A}x^{*}+\hat{s}=\hat{b}`$ with $`\hat{s}\in K`$, and
$`\Omega^{*}=\hat{c}^{\top}x^{*}`$. Since $`y\in K^{*}`$ and
$`\hat{s}\in K`$, $`\left\langle y,\ \hat{s}\right\rangle\geq 0`$, hence

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\hat{c}^{\top}x^{*}\geq\hat{c}^{\top}x^{*}-\left\langle y,\ \hat{s}\right\rangle=\hat{c}^{\top}x^{*}-\left\langle y,\ \hat{b}-\hat{A}x^{*}\right\rangle=-\hat{b}^{\top}y+(\hat{c}+\hat{A}^{\top}y)^{\top}x^{*}.
``` |  |

Now replace intended data by floating data plus a bounded perturbation.
Writing $`\hat{A}=A+\Delta_{A}`$, $`\hat{b}=b+\Delta_{b}`$,
$`\hat{c}=c+\Delta_{c}`$ with the stated elementwise bounds,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
-\hat{b}^{\top}y=-b^{\top}y-\Delta_{b}^{\top}y\geq-b^{\top}y-\varepsilon_{b}\lVert y\rVert_{1},
``` |  |

and

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
(\hat{c}+\hat{A}^{\top}y)^{\top}x^{*}=(c+A^{\top}y)^{\top}x^{*}+(\Delta_{c}+\Delta_{A}^{\top}y)^{\top}x^{*}\geq-\big(\lVert c+A^{\top}y\rVert_{\infty}+\varepsilon_{A}\lVert y\rVert_{1}+\varepsilon_{c}\big)\lVert x^{*}\rVert_{1},
``` |  |

using Hölder’s inequality
$`\lvert w^{\top}x^{*}\rvert\leq\lVert w\rVert_{\infty}\lVert x^{*}\rVert_{1}`$,
the residual bound $`\lVert c+A^{\top}y\rVert_{\infty}\leq r`$, and the
elementwise bounds
$`\lVert\Delta_{A}^{\top}y\rVert_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon_{A}\lVert y\rVert_{1}`$,
$`\lVert\Delta_{c}\rVert_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon_{c}`$. Combining and
using $`\lVert x^{*}\rVert_{1}\leq X`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Omega^{*}=\hat{c}^{\top}x^{*}\geq-b^{\top}y-\big(r+\varepsilon_{A}\lVert y\rVert_{1}+\varepsilon_{c}\big)X-\varepsilon_{b}\lVert y\rVert_{1}=-b^{\top}y-\Pi.
``` |  |

Evaluating $`-b^{\top}y`$ with downward rounding and $`\Pi`$ with upward
rounding only decreases the right-hand side, so $`\Omega^{*}\geq L`$. ∎

### C.3 A-priori bound on $`\lVert x^{*}\rVert_{1}`$

The constant $`X`$ is computed in the *CVXPY-canonicalised* coordinates,
block by block, with all arithmetic outward-rounded in interval form;
the routines return the upper endpoint.

###### Theorem C.2 (Primal bound, $`C_{6.5}`$).

Let $`L=2/N`$ and let $`\varepsilon`$ be the equality tolerance. Every
primal-feasible point $`x`$ of the overlap program satisfies
$`\|x\|_{1}\leq X_{6.5}`$, where $`X_{6.5}`$ is the outward-rounded sum
of the block bounds established in the proof.

###### Proof.

We bound each block from its governing constraint.

*Objective.* The objective variable contributes $`\Omega\leq 1`$, since
$`\Omega\leq 1`$ is imposed directly (an average overlap cannot exceed
$`1`$).

*Mass.* From the normalization
$`L\sum_{j}(w_{j}+v_{j})\leq 1+\varepsilon`$ and $`w_{j},v_{j}\geq 0`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\|w\|_{1}+\|v\|_{1}=\sum_{j}(w_{j}+v_{j})\leq\frac{1+\varepsilon}{L}=\frac{N(1+\varepsilon)}{2}.
``` |  |

*Fourier coefficients.* The Parseval constraint gives
$`|c_{k}|,|d_{k}|\leq 2/\pi`$, and there are $`T`$ of each, so
$`\|c\|_{1}+\|d\|_{1}\leq\tfrac{2}{\pi}\cdot 2T=\tfrac{4T}{\pi}`$.

*Derived moments.* The coefficients $`a_{m},b_{m}`$ are entries of the
positive-semidefinite moment matrix associated with $`f`$: $`a_{m}`$ and
$`b_{m}`$ are the real and imaginary parts of an off-diagonal entry
$`(T^{f})_{ij}`$ at lag $`|i-j|=m`$. For a PSD matrix the off-diagonal
entries are controlled by the diagonal,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
|(T^{f})_{ij}|\;\leq\;\sqrt{(T^{f})_{ii}\,(T^{f})_{jj}}\;\leq\;\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl((T^{f})_{ii}+(T^{f})_{jj}\bigr),
``` |  |

and each diagonal entry is a zeroth moment of a measure of total mass at
most $`2`$, so $`(T^{f})_{ii}\leq 2`$ and therefore
$`|a_{m}|,|b_{m}|\leq 2`$. With at most $`2R`$ indices for each of $`a`$
and $`b`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\|a\|_{1}\leq 2\cdot 2R=4R,\qquad\|b\|_{1}\leq 4R,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad\|a\|_{1}+\|b\|_{1}\leq 8R.
``` |  |

*Truncation slacks.* The slacks are bounded in closed form by

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
|\varepsilon_{2m-1}|\leq\frac{2(2m-1)}{\pi\bigl(4-((2m-1)/T)^{2}\bigr)\sqrt{6T^{3}}},\qquad|\delta_{2m-1}|\leq\frac{4}{\pi\bigl(4-((2m-1)/T)^{2}\bigr)\sqrt{2T}},
``` |  |

for $`1\leq m\leq R`$ (the hypothesis $`R\leq T`$ keeps each denominator
positive); their $`\ell_{1}`$ contribution is the sum of these closed
forms, evaluated in interval arithmetic.

*Canonicalization auxiliaries.* Conic canonicalization introduces $`4R`$
square epigraph variables, each bounded by $`4`$ since
$`a_{m},b_{m}\in[-2,2]`$; two sum-of-squares epigraphs, each bounded by
$`4T/\pi^{2}`$ from the Parseval budget; and $`4R+1`$ absolute-value
slacks, each bounded by the tolerance $`\varepsilon`$.

Summing all contributions and rounding outward gives
$`X_{6.5}\geq\|x^{\star}\|_{1}`$. ∎

###### Theorem C.3 (Primal bound, $`C_{6.2}`$).

Let $`\omega=\Omega_{\mathrm{ub}}-1`$ with $`\Omega_{\mathrm{ub}}=2`$.
Every primal-feasible point $`x`$ of the autocorrelation program
satisfies $`\|x\|_{1}\leq X_{6.2}`$, where $`X_{6.2}`$ is the
outward-rounded sum of the block bounds established in the proof.

###### Proof.

The cap $`\Omega\leq\Omega_{\mathrm{ub}}=2`$ holds because the program’s
optimum lies below the best known upper bound on $`C_{6.2}`$, so
$`\omega=\Omega_{\mathrm{ub}}-1\geq\Omega-1\geq 0`$. We bound each
variable block in turn.

*Objective and mass.* The objective variable satisfies
$`\Omega\leq\Omega_{\mathrm{ub}}=2`$. The simplex constraint
$`\sum_{j}p_{j}=1`$ with $`p_{j}\geq 0`$ gives $`\|p\|_{1}=1`$.

*Moments.* The envelope constraints
$`\gamma^{-}_{k}\!\cdot p\leq a_{k}\leq\gamma^{+}_{k}\!\cdot p`$ and the
bound $`|\gamma^{\pm}_{k}|\leq 1`$ (cosine enclosures) give
$`|a_{k}|\leq\sum_{j}p_{j}=1`$ for each of the $`K+2`$ indices
$`k=0,\dots,K+1`$, so $`\|a\|_{1}\leq K+2`$; likewise
$`\|b\|_{1}\leq K+1`$.

*Moment matrix.* We first bound the trace. The energy constraint
$`\Omega\geq 1+2\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}v_{k}`$ together with the cap gives

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}v_{k}\;\leq\;\tfrac{1}{2}(\Omega-1)\;\leq\;\tfrac{\omega}{2}.
``` |  |

The slack constraint $`v_{k}\geq(M_{kk}+M_{K+k,K+k})^{2}`$ and the
nonnegativity of the diagonal of the PSD matrix $`M`$ give
$`M_{kk}+M_{K+k,K+k}\leq\sqrt{v_{k}}`$, so by Cauchy–Schwarz,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{k=1}^{K}\bigl(M_{kk}+M_{K+k,K+k}\bigr)\;\leq\;\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sqrt{v_{k}}\;\leq\;\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^{K}\tfrac{1}{w_{k}}\Bigr)^{1/2}\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}v_{k}\Bigr)^{1/2}\;\leq\;\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^{K}\tfrac{1}{w_{k}}\Bigr)^{1/2}\sqrt{\tfrac{\omega}{2}}.
``` |  |

The Fejér weights are $`w_{k}=\tfrac{K+1-k}{K+1}`$, so
$`\tfrac{1}{w_{k}}=\tfrac{K+1}{K+1-k}\leq K+1`$ for $`1\leq k\leq K`$,
whence $`\sum_{k=1}^{K}\tfrac{1}{w_{k}}\leq K(K+1)`$. With $`M_{00}=1`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\tr M\;=\;1+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\bigl(M_{kk}+M_{K+k,K+k}\bigr)\;\leq\;1+\sqrt{\tfrac{K(K+1)\,\omega}{2}}.
``` |  |

For the vectorized block, $`M\succeq 0`$ gives
$`|M_{ij}|\leq\sqrt{M_{ii}M_{jj}}\leq\tfrac{1}{2}(M_{ii}+M_{jj})`$. The
symmetric vectorization has entries $`M_{ii}`$ on the diagonal and
$`\sqrt{2}\,M_{ij}`$ off-diagonal, so each diagonal entry $`M_{ii}`$
enters the off-diagonal sum with total weight
$`\sqrt{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot(\text{number of partners})\leq\tfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,(2K)`$.
Hence

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\|\svec(M)\|_{1}=\sum_{i}M_{ii}+\sqrt{2}\!\sum_{i<j}|M_{ij}|\leq\bigl(1+\sqrt{2}\,K\bigr)\tr M.
``` |  |

*Slacks and epigraph.* From $`\sum_{k}w_{k}v_{k}\leq\omega/2`$ and
$`w_{k}\leq 1`$ we obtain $`\|v\|_{1}=\sum_{k}v_{k}`$; using
$`w_{k}\geq w_{K}=\tfrac{1}{K+1}`$ this is bounded by
$`(K+1)\sum_{k}w_{k}v_{k}\leq(K+1)\omega/2`$. The epigraph auxiliary
cannot exceed $`\|v\|_{1}`$ by its defining inequality.

*Hermitian block.* The constraint $`\operatorname{tr}Q=\Omega-1=\omega`$
together with $`Q\succeq 0`$ gives $`\sum_{i}Q_{ii}=\omega`$, and the
same PSD/vectorization argument as for $`M`$ yields
$`\|\herm(Q)\|_{1}\leq\bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt{2}\,K}{2}\bigr)\omega`$, the
$`\sqrt{2}`$ again being the off-diagonal scaling of the vectorization.

Summing the block bounds - $`\Omega_{\mathrm{ub}}`$, $`1`$, $`K+2`$,
$`K+1`$, $`(1+\sqrt{2}K)\tr M`$ with
$`\tr M\leq 1+\sqrt{K(K+1)\omega/2}`$, $`(K+1)\omega/2`$ (twice, for
$`v`$ and the epigraph), and $`(1+\tfrac{\sqrt{2}K}{2})\omega`$ - each
rounded outward, gives $`X_{6.2}\geq\|x^{\star}\|_{1}`$. ∎

### C.4 Rigorous certificate of dual-cone containment

It remains to verify $`y\in K^{*}`$. We walk the product cone in SCS
order using directed-rounding interval arithmetic (the mpmath interval
type iv). The nonnegative and second-order cones are self-dual; the PSD
cone is self-dual and is certified by a residual-plus-spectral-bound
test: a floating Cholesky factor $`L`$ furnishes a rigorous lower bound
on $`\lambda_{\min}(LL^{\top})`$ through the exact inverse $`B=L^{-1}`$,
and the discrepancy between $`LL^{\top}`$ and the block is absorbed by a
rigorous residual bound, the two combined by Weyl’s inequality.

0:  candidate dual $`y`$; cone dimensions
$`(\dim_{\mathrm{zero}},\dim_{\geq 0},\{q_{i}\},\{n_{j}\})`$; PSD shift
$`\sigma>0`$; precision dps

0:  ok (all blocks certified) and a rigorous margin per block

1:  Zero cone: the dual is free; skip.

2:  Nonnegative cone: verify $`\min_{i}y_{i}\geq 0`$ by floating
comparison (the float value is itself the witness); margin
$`\leftarrow\min_{i}y_{i}`$.

3:  Second-order cones $`y=(t,z)`$: interval-enclose
$`\|z\|_{2}=\sqrt{\sum_{k}z_{k}^{2}}`$ and verify
$`(t-\|z\|_{2})_{\downarrow}>0`$; margin
$`\leftarrow(t-\|z\|_{2})_{\downarrow}`$.

4:  PSD cones ($`n_{j}\times n_{j}`$): reshape the SCS $`\svec`$ block
to a symmetric $`Y`$ (off-diagonals divided by $`\sqrt{2}`$), then:

5:   (a) attempt a floating Cholesky of
$`A_{\mathrm{mid}}=\tfrac{1}{2}(Y+Y^{\top})-\sigma I`$, retaining the
computed lower factor $`L`$; return fail if it does not complete;

6:   (b) form the exact interval inverse $`B=L^{-1}`$ by triangular
forward substitution and $`C=B^{\top}B=(LL^{\top})^{-1}`$; bound
$`\lambda_{\max}(C)\leq\lambda_{\max}^{+}`$ by Gershgorin, giving the
rigorous bound $`\lambda_{\min}(LL^{\top})\geq 1/\lambda_{\max}^{+}`$;

7:   (c) rigorously enclose the residual $`E=(A-\sigma I)-LL^{\top}`$ in
Frobenius norm over the interval $`A_{ij}\in[Y_{ij}-\rho,Y_{ij}+\rho]`$,
obtaining $`\|E\|_{F}^{+}\geq\|E\|_{2}`$;

8:   (d) certify with margin
$`m=\sigma+1/\lambda_{\max}^{+}-\|E\|_{F}^{+}`$, a rigorous lower bound
on $`\lambda_{\min}(A)`$; the block passes iff $`m>0`$.

9:  return ok $`=`$ (all blocks certified), with the per-block margins.
````
